prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080, drawn as a FULL-BLEED EDGE-TO-EDGE illustration.

FRAMING - READ THIS FIRST: There is NO page border. Do NOT draw a rectangle, a double rule, a thin outer line, a box, a panel edge or any margin band around the drawing. The scene is BIGGER than the square and the square CROPS it: the intestinal tube, the carpet of villi and the background elements must run right off the TOP edge, the BOTTOM edge, the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge with white space only where the drawing itself leaves it. The very first pixel row and column on all four sides must be part of the artwork or plain white - never a drawn line.

SCENE: A friendly cartoon ROTAVIRUS character sitting inside a giant cartoon SMALL INTESTINE shown in simple cut-away side view, so we look down the inside of the tube. The rotavirus is a chunky round ball with a smooth outer rim; all the way around the rim sit about eighteen SHORT, THICK, BLUNT STUDS, each a small rounded bump that is WIDER THAN IT IS LONG and sits directly on the rim with no stalk, no stem and no neck - like the squat teeth of a cog wheel or the studs on a toy tractor tyre. The whole character therefore reads as a friendly toy WAGON WHEEL with stubby spokes. Each stud is a closed rounded shape a child can colour in; they must never be thin lines, spikes, pins, rays or anything radiating. Inside the rim, draw two more simple concentric rings so you can see it is built of three nested shells, and a small bundle of short rounded rods in the middle for its genes. The rotavirus has a BIG FRIENDLY FACE: two large round eyes with pupils, cheerful curved eyebrows and a wide sheepish grin, plus two little stubby arms, one of them waving.
Around it in the same scene: the inner wall of the intestine runs right across the picture and off both side edges as rows of tall soft finger-shaped VILLI, like a shaggy carpet, and two of them are smiling cell characters with simple happy faces; a big chunky cartoon MEDICINE DROPPER (a fat pipette with a squeezy bulb) tips in from the top-left corner, its handle running off the top edge, with three big round outlined DROPS falling from its tip toward the virus - the swallowed vaccine; and on the right a large chunky WATER BOTTLE with a bendy straw and a happy face, its top running off the top-right edge, with two more big round outlined drops beside it. Everything is drawn large, simple and chunky so a child can colour inside every shape.

STYLE - coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with generous white space inside them.
- Playful and reassuring - nothing gruesome, no sick child, no toilet, no vomit, no needles.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN - the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, double rule, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box or vignette anywhere near the edges of the square. NO frame of any kind.
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion lines or halo of rays behind, around or under the character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere on the page. The virus's studs must stay short, blunt, closed and clearly attached to a solid rim so the character never reads as a burst or a star.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO lipid envelope or membrane around the virus, NO long spikes, NO tail, NO legs beyond the two little stubby arms.
